question: How do I log in to the cluster for the first time?
reference_answer: Log in at my.nesi.org.nz, then go to OnDemand, which redirects to your institution's Tuakiri login. On first login you set up MFA by scanning a QR code in an authenticator app and entering the 6-digit code it generates. You're then asked whether to trust the device — trusting it skips the 6-digit code for 7 days; don't trust shared or private-browsing machines.

How do I request more memory for a Slurm job?
reference_answer: Use --mem to request memory per node — the right choice for serial, multithreaded, and MPI jobs evenly split across nodes. --mem-per-cpu (memory per logical CPU) is only preferred for MPI jobs randomly placed across more than one node with tasks split unevenly.

question: My job died with 'Detected 1 oom-kill event(s)' — what does that mean?
reference_answer: OOM means Out Of Memory: your job tried to use more RAM than Slurm reserved for it, so the kernel killed it. This can happen even if sacct doesn't show high usage, since accounting only samples every 30 seconds and ignores memory-backed /tmp or $TMPDIR usage. Fix it by increasing --mem in your submission script, or by making the job less memory-intensive.

question: How do I submit a Slurm job array?
reference_answer: Add --array to your #SBATCH header, e.g. --array=1-2, and the same script runs once per index. Inside the script, use the environment variable $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to vary behaviour between tasks (as a function argument, an index into an array, or a random seed); in the Slurm header itself, use %a instead since env vars don't expand there. The maximum array size is 1000 tasks — contact support for more.

What are my filesystem quotas and how do I check them?
reference_answer: Run storage_quota to see your usage and allocations (updated hourly). Default quotas are 20 GB for /home, 100 GB for /nesi/project, and 10 TB for /nesi/nobackup (scratch); Freezer has no fixed quota.

question: Are files in nobackup deleted automatically?
reference_answer: Yes. Files in /nesi/nobackup that have been untouched (not created, accessed, or modified) for 90 days are deleted automatically, with no exceptions. You're notified by email 2 weeks (at the 76-day mark) before deletion. Run nn_doomed_list to see which of your files are currently scheduled for deletion.
